title: London home renovation finds 17th-century shoes and 4 dried chickens behind wall
content: In a fascinating archaeological find at Lauderdale House, London, a wicker basket dating back to the 17th century was unearthed, revealing hidden objects like broken shoes. These artifacts were once believed to safeguard homes from malevolent spirits. The discovery, which also included four chickens, sheds light on post-medieval England's unique customs aimed at protecting households from supernatural threats and tells a fascinating story of domestic life.

title: India's biggest enemy at Hagley Oval? Poor catching, poorer shot selection

With Dhruv Jurel left facing a mountain, India are staring at a collapse that was largely self-inflicted.

Psychology says putting off important tasks may be about emotions, not laziness
content: Many people struggle with procrastination, resulting in guilt and anxiety. Studies show that emotional regulation is crucial in understanding this tendency. A helpful method to combat procrastination involves dividing tasks into smaller, manageable steps. By recognizing and managing the emotions tied to these tasks, individuals can enhance their productivity. Gaining insight into the emotional triggers of procrastination can empower individuals to tackle this common issue effectively.
